bucket_reason: Observe is done at MED confidence: the mechanism is exact, but the non-halting invariant is not closed, so proof work waits.
question: W4-5 (469) and its same-table sibling 599 have an exact macro model where halting needs one parity defect: fund one ~2 h stage to search for an inductive context invariant, or park both?

options.label: Fund one ~2 h invariant-search stage for 469 + 599
options.consequence: Build an abstract-interpretation closure over the validated macro model (abstract tokens P1/P2/P3+, Z1/Z3/Z5+, D, block classes; bigram or regular context language), plus a wider TM-level CTL sweep. Output: an inductive INV (then proof.md and formalization) or a precise obstruction, then park.

options.label: Park 469 and 599 now
options.consequence: No compute. Both go to STUCK with the macro model, validators and INV census in scripts/. Resume if a chaotic-class invariant method appears.

options.label: Write proof.md now with a hand-made invariant
options.consequence: Open-ended: the simple side conditions already fail random closure (~2% of steps) and one strengthening fails on the real run at step 2,403,364, so a hand guess is likely to need several rounds.

rationale: Exact model (all E-events from blank, 12,000 random, step formulas): a search over it is cheap and checkable.
Halting has one route (a C-pass meeting 0^2); parity already closes, only local context is open.
One result covers 469 and 599; park if the closure finds no invariant.

evidence.text: Fig 2: sweeps at the block/pair interface (every step from an E-event at step 36,312).
Macro model vs TM: 34,479,962/34,479,962 E-events to 1e9 (start A), 1,032,103/1,032,103 to 3e7 (start D = 599); random 6,000/6,000 INV-shaped + 6,000/6,000 wild.
Parity census: closed blocks even, r and every zero run odd at all 1,722,791 E-events to 5e7.
Not inductive yet: random closure from INV states leaves INV in ~2% of steps, all via r = 1 (lone-1 creation).

effort_if_yes: ~2 h agent time, 1-2 light Python processes (the macro model runs ~1e6 TM-steps/s).
